name: Learn beginner poi spinning
blurb: Two weighted balls on cords, spun in patterns. The four beginner patterns — same-time, split-time, butterfly and weaves — are all combinations of two circles and a timing.
gear: Sock poi or practice poi (never fire poi while learning)
Room to swing with arms fully extended
steps: Learn the basic forward and reverse spin with one poi in each hand, keeping the planes flat beside your body.
Learn same-time and split-time: both poi at the same point of the circle, then exactly opposite.
Learn the butterfly, where both poi spin in a plane in front of you, passing each other.
Learn the three-beat weave — the pattern where your arms cross alternately — first with one poi, then two.
Practise the transitions between these four patterns rather than just the patterns themselves.
Film yourself: planes look much messier on camera than they feel.
tips: You will hit yourself. Sock poi means it stings for a second instead of bruising.
Keep the planes clean and parallel; the visual effect is almost entirely about plane discipline.
Never progress to fire poi without an experienced spotter, a fire blanket and natural-fibre clothing.
proof: You move between butterfly and a three-beat weave, both directions, without tangling.
